column1: # *** ⚠ THIS FILE WAS POLLUTED BY ITS OWN TEST SUITE. FOUND AND FIXED 2026-09-10. ***
# `dice.roll()` logs by DEFAULT -- correct for play, because this file is the
# evidence -- so EVERY `pytest tools/tests` run wrote 31 rows into it. It had been
# doing that for as long as those tests existed. Found while checking whether the
# log was current before a compact: the tail held attack rolls for a giant centipede
# and an orc that no character in this campaign has ever met.
# SCALE: the test rows include 5 "giant centipede attacks AC 9" and 1 "orc attacks
# AC 9" per run. Those markers count 625 and 125, which agree exactly: 125 RUNS,
# about 3,875 rows, in a file of 7,247. MORE THAN HALF THIS FILE IS TEST OUTPUT.
# HOW TO TELL THEM APART: play rows carry a reason that names the day or the
# expedition ("day 69: ..."). Test rows are terse and carry no exped and no turn --
# "morale", "giant centipede attacks AC 9", "F save vs Spell", "wandering check,
# anchor 20", "initiative, party". Some of those strings DO occur in real play, so
# no single grep separates them cleanly; the centipede and orc lines are unique to
# the suite.
# THE LEAK IS CLOSED: tools/tests/conftest.py redirects dice.ROLLS to a scratch file
# for the whole session, and tools/tests/test_no_roll_log_leak.py is the alarm --
# it rolls a die and asserts this file's size did not move.
# THE EXISTING 3,875 ROWS ARE STILL HERE, DELIBERATELY. This log is append-only by
# doctrine and purging it is the player's call, not the DM's. Nothing has been
# deleted.
# Every die rolled, appended automatically by tools/dice.py and tools/combat.py.
# This exists so a disputed sequence can be checked without grepping a 60 MB
# conversation transcript, which is how the encounter log had to be rebuilt
# once. It is an audit trail, not a source of record: nothing reads it back.
# `hidden` marks a roll made in advance and concealed — in practice only the
# wandering-check jitter, which is reported to the player once it fires.

day 102: THE NORTH ROAD, a full day's travel, DAY AFTER MARKET so there is traffic going home. *** ROAD ENCOUNTERS IN THIS CAMPAIGN ARE PEOPLE, not monsters -- the precedent is day 6, 'the patrol begins, Osk met on the road', and the party has walked or ridden this road on days 96, 99 and 100 without incident. *** AND THE PARTY IS CONSPICUOUS TODAY: one cart and three horses carrying 1,022 lb of iron and smith's tools, in a hundred where the layoffs are upstream of the robberies and where four of the party's own people are ex-bandits off this very road. *** Bands: 1-2 ordinary traffic and nothing that stops them; 3-4 somebody they know, and it is worth the halt; 5 the PATROL, which has its own weight; 6 somebody takes an interest in the load.

day 100 market, resolved now: DID HASK ASK COLL FOR SARN TO KEEP THE RECORD, as he was told to? *** THIS IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS AND IT IS NOT A LOYALTY TEST, IT IS A COMPETENCE ONE: Hask CANNOT READ OR RECKON (d6=2, day 98) and the party knows it, which is exactly why the clerk was named and not left to his judgement. DAVE STOOD SURETY FOR THIS MAN PERSONALLY, with his purse and his name, and then handed him a cart of goods and the takings. *** 1-2 he did not, and sold it out of his head; 3-4 he got Sarn and the record exists; 5-6 he got Sarn AND did something more than he was asked.

day 100 market: DID HASK ASK WEND ABOUT THE KETTLE BEFORE SELLING IT, and what did she say? *** He was told plainly: ask her first, hold it aside if she says so. 1,800 gp-weight of cast iron with a chain and a swivel is not ordinary salvage and Wend is the FACTOR of the hundred. *** 1-2 he did not ask and it went with the rest; 3-4 he asked and she said SELL; 5-6 he asked and SHE WANTED IT HELD, and has a reason.

day 100 market: HOW DID THE SELLING GO for 421 lb of crag salvage -- chain, thirteen shovels, a smith's whole kit, a 12-inch vise, fifteen chisels, a mason's and a cobbler's toolbox, hand bellows, sixty unfletched arrows, thirteen pots and pans? *** MARKET DAY, and the party's own at-cost board already sets what iron goes for in this hundred, which cuts both ways. 1-2 slow, much of it unsold and sitting in Wend's barn; 3-4 most of it went, at honest prices; 5-6 it went well and somebody took the lot.

day 100 market: WHAT THE LOT FETCHED. *** NO 1e BOOK PRICES ANY OF IT and assets.tsv records only weights, so this is a DM call on a declared basis, and the basis is: worked tools are worth far more than their iron. The party's own bar iron runs about 0.25 gp/lb (29 bars estimated at 150 gross); a smith's whole hand-tool set, a 12-inch vise, fifteen chisels, two trade toolboxes, seventy feet of heavy chain, thirteen shovels, a 150 lb cast kettle with chain and swivel, thirteen pots and pans, a sheave block and sixty unfletched arrows are NOT bar iron. *** Anchored against the campaign's own salvage sales -- the SD barrel at 58, the bronze wrestlers at 115. ROLL: 4d10 + 100, so 104-140 gp, and d6=5 already said it went well and somebody took the lot.

day 100 market: WHO TOOK THE LOT? 1-3 MUND THE SMITH -- the ironmongery is squarely his and he is the only man in the hundred who buys iron by weight and sells it by the piece; 4-5 a dealer up from the southern road for market day, gone by now; 6 split between two or three and Hask cannot say clearly which.

day 102: HOW AN EVEN SPLIT OF THE 117 LANDS ON HASK. *** articles.md's gifts-fail-work-lands table has a DIRECT entry: 'Hask, asked to PICK his share in front of Wend -- 24 -- badly.' Gifts land badly on low-standing dependents; work lands. *** BUT THE DISTINCTION IS REAL AND IT FAVOURS THE PARTY: that 24 was a man ASKED TO CHOOSE, put on the spot in front of the factor of the hundred. THIS IS AN EVEN SPLIT STATED, NOT OFFERED -- thirteen gold each, everybody the same, no choosing and nobody singled out. *** AND HE EARNED THIS ONE. He carted it down, he sold it, he got 117 for it and handed it over whole. It is not a kindness put on a man with nothing to give back; it is his cut of a job he did. *** +30 for that: the same figures gave 100 and 109 when he was handed a DECISION and a JOB. DMG p.63.

day 102: THE SAME SPLIT ON DELLIE AND ISTA. *** Dellie went south with Hask and is 'sharp, says little, means it'; Ista's table entry is 'offered the loom -- 9 -- badly' against 'GIVEN THE LANTERN AS A DUTY -- 71 -- well'. *** Same +30 reasoning: this is a cut of work, evenly stated, nobody asked to choose and nobody singled out. DMG p.63.

day 102: MUND, SECOND DEALING. *** Reaction 52 on day 97 -- NEUTRAL, a tradesman selling to strangers with money. Since then he has BOUGHT THEIR WHOLE SALVAGE LOT FOR 117 GP at the day-100 market, unprompted and without haggling, which is a substantial vote of confidence in their goods. *** +15 for a completed transaction of that size in his favour. DMG p.63. Dave CHA 10, no adjustment.

day 102: DOES MUND RAISE THE PARTY'S OWN AT-COST BOARD when they ask him to buy 609 lb of bar iron? *** THIS IS NOT A DM-SIDE SECRET AND IT IS THE PARTY'S OWN DOING: they sell iron, nails and salt AT COST on a board OPEN TO ANYBODY, as a matter of policy, in this hundred. assets.tsv prices a comparable 600 lb load at 100 gp at Ludbury and nearer 160 LAID DOWN. So the party is asking a man to pay for bar iron at a price its own public board undercuts. *** HE IS A SMITH. HE WILL NOTICE. The question is only whether he SAYS SO. *** 1-2 he offers low and does not explain; 3-4 HE SAYS IT PLAINLY -- points at the board and asks why he should pay more; 5-6 he says it plainly AND has a proposal that gets round it. *** ⚠ NOTHING HERE REVEALS THE SEALED d6=6. Knowing the board's price is not the same as admitting he buys off it in quantity, and the board is public.

day 102: THE TWENTY FEET OF FINE COPPER WIRE -- off the area 13 rack, about an ounce of metal. Toller sent them to Mund for it and called it a smith's business. 1-2 he has no use for it and says so; 3-4 he takes it for a token; 5-6 he wants it and it is worth more than they think.

day 102: WHAT MUND OFFERS FOR THE 29 BARS -- 609 lb of bar iron. *** ANCHORED ON THE PARTY'S OWN BOARD, which is the argument he has just made out loud: assets.tsv iron_salt records a comparable 600 lb load at 100 gp AT LUDBURY -- and the board sells at the LUDBURY price, which is the whole reason 'at cost' ran 50-70 gp BELOW cost (articles.md fourth finding). So the board's rate for this weight is ABOUT 100 GP and he can have it at that any time the party's carts come south. *** WHY HE WOULD PAY ANYTHING ABOVE IT: 609 lb standing in front of him TODAY, in one lot, with no waiting on a Ludbury run. Convenience has a price and he is at reaction 99. *** 2d10 + 90, so 92-110.

day 102: THE TWENTY FEET OF FINE COPPER WIRE. d6=5 -- he wants it and it is worth more than the party thinks. *** WHY: about an ounce of metal, but FINE DRAWN WIRE IS LABOUR, not material. Nobody in the north hundred draws wire; it comes up from a city or it does not come at all, and a smith who needs a few inches for a repair cannot make it himself in an afternoon. *** 2d4 gp for twenty feet, against a DM weight call of half a gp-weight the foot recorded on day 95.

day 102 REDONE: WHAT DOES MUND ARGUE NOW, with the board repriced? *** THE OLD ROLLS ARE VOID: d6=4 'he points at the board and asks why he should pay more' and 2d10+90=99 gp both rested on a board reading ~100 for 600 lb. It reads ~160 laid down. HIS OWN SENTENCE NOW ARGUES FOR THE HIGHER NUMBER. *** KEPT: reaction 99, and that he wants the copper wire at 5 gp -- neither depends on the board. *** ⚠ AND HE MUST STAY GUARDED. The day-97 DM note predicted exactly this: 'the moment that board carries two numbers, MUND'S INPUT COST RISES and he is the customer who will notice first and mind most.' HE HAS NOTICED. But a trader does not volunteer his own costs, and the sealed d6=6 -- that he buys the party's at-cost bar IN QUANTITY and sells it on worked -- must not leak. Knowing a public board's price is not admitting how much you buy off it. *** 1-2 he says nothing about the board at all and simply offers; 3-4 he allows that iron has got dearer, no more; 5-6 he says more than he means to.

day 102 REDONE: MUND'S OFFER FOR THE 29 BARS, 609 lb, against a repriced board. *** HIS ALTERNATIVE SOURCE IS THAT BOARD AND IT NOW READS ~160 LAID DOWN for a comparable 600 lb. He will not pay above his alternative; he would like a discount for taking 609 lb in one lot today with no waiting on a Ludbury run, which is worth real money to a smith. *** AND HE IS NOT A GRINDER: reaction 99, and two days ago he took the whole salvage lot at 117 without haggling. *** 2d10 + 135, so 137-155 -- a 5 to 23 gp discount off his own alternative cost.

day 103: HOW MUCH LAMP OIL IS IN WETHERSBY? *** The party has ZERO SEALED FLASKS -- all eight went to Durnhak on the 101st -- and 32.6 turns of oil left in two lamps and nothing behind them. *** LAST TIME THEY ASKED, DAY 97: d6=2 then d2=2, TWO FLASKS, and that was every flask in the town. Six days and one market day (the 100th) have passed since. *** Bands: 1-2 the town is still dry, 1d2 flasks and no more; 3-4 the market restocked it, 1d4+2; 5-6 a carrier came up the southern road with a proper consignment, 2d4+4. *** THIS IS A SMALL MARKET TOWN IN THE NORTH HUNDRED IN EARLY SPRING and oil is imported; the party's own carts are the district's usual way of getting such things, which is the joke.

day 103: d6=1, THE TOWN IS STILL DRY. How many flasks at all -- 1d2. *** WETHERSBY HAS NO OIL TO SPEAK OF AND HAS NOT SINCE THE PARTY LAST ASKED. This is not the DM squeezing them: the town had exactly two on the 97th and the party bought both, the 100th was a market and it did not fix it, and OIL IS IMPORTED INTO THIS HUNDRED ON THE PARTY'S OWN CARTS -- which is the whole joke and also L024's shape. They are the supply line, so when they are short, so is everyone.
